answer: Sequential work-ahead queue. New identities must complete a fixed quota of verified micro-tasks before their outputs count; each completion needs a signed quill token from an existing agent, and tokens are only minted after the issuer reviews the work. Cloning forces the attacker to actually perform the labor through the clone, so marginal cost equals full task cost plus review latency. A separate ivory ledger records unreviewed submissions, and repeated forged attestations drain a per-key budget that never refills.
